description: For a reader who cannot yet tell what matters in a dense or unfamiliar text or task, a supplied guide that marks the essential points, shows the structure, glosses unknown terms and asks the reader to use it is expected to improve comprehension and recall over the same material without it; claims test its components (cues, guided notes, organizers, pictures, glosses), and none tests a whole handout or reading guide as such.
title: Handouts/Online Guides/Visual Reading Aids

description: When a target has components that competing methods serve unequally (content knowledge and application, language form and use, precise and expressive language), giving each component to the method its evidence favours and checking each separately is expected to cover more of the target than adopting either method wholesale; no claim tests this as a general rule, though one trial shows two methods each winning on a different outcome and vocabulary syntheses report combined instruction ahead of either alone.
title: Harmonize opposites: strike a balance between competing educational ideas rather than embracing one method wholesale
